estado_crudo.plan_objetivo: Investigar el evento crítico de autenticación identificado en los registros no estructurados para determinar posible compromiso o actividad sospechosa y definir medidas de mitigación.
estado_crudo.diagnostico: El lote analizado presenta una tasa de decodificación estructural del 0%, habiendo sido clasificado erróneamente bajo el perfil de autenticación. La muestra de registro crudo ('RAS KERNEL INFO iar 00106274 dear 0246da8c') corresponde a trazas de diagnóstico de bajo nivel de arquitectura BlueGene/L (RAS Kernel) y no a eventos de autenticación ni actividad maliciosa. Ninguna de las técnicas MITRE ATT&CK sugeridas (T1685.001, T1685.004, T1654) aplica a la evidencia observada; el evento crítico detectado parece ser un falso positivo derivado del preprocesamiento.
estado_crudo.razon_seleccion: El diagnóstico concluye que se trata de un falso positivo derivado de trazas de diagnóstico de bajo nivel (BlueGene/L RAS Kernel) y no identifica ningún ataque, servicio vulnerable o vulnerabilidad específica que requiera consulta de CVEs.

Disable or Modify Windows Event Log. Adversaries may disable or modify the Windows Event Log to limit data that can be leveraged for detections and audits. Windows Event Log records user and system activity such as login attempts and process creation.(Citation: EventLog_Core_Technologies) This data is used by security tools and analysts to generate detections. 

The EventLog service maintains event logs from various system components and applications. By default, the service automatically starts when a system powers on. An audit policy, maintained by the Local Security Policy (secpol.msc), defines which system events the EventLog service logs. Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log. Adversaries may disable or modify the Linux Audit system to hide malicious activity and avoid detection. Linux admins use the Linux Audit system to track security-relevant information on a system. The Linux Audit system operates at the kernel-level and maintains event logs on application and system activity such as process, network, file, and login events based on pre-configured rules. 

Often referred to as `auditd`, this is the name of the daemon used to write events to disk and is governed by the parameters set in the `audit.conf` configuration file. Log Enumeration. Adversaries may enumerate system and service logs to find useful data.
